author: Good Enough
description:
Patients were injected with insulin until they slipped into comas... and this was considered “treatment.”

In early insane asylums, insulin shock therapy was used to repeatedly induce comas in patients, sometimes for months at a time. Doctors believed these extreme episodes could treat mental illness, despite the serious risks and physical toll it took on the body.

This video explores one of the most disturbing practices in medical history and what patients were forced to endure.
